title: Make planning enforce owner priority order, with a check
summary: Root cause: plan ordering in crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs only honours a per-request `Priority:` line or priority record, so owner priorities stated in BRIEF.md addenda never reach the plan, and nothing checks the built order against them. Fix at plan construction: an owner-priority input ranks rungs ahead of default order, and a check flags a plan whose top-priority item is not in the first wave. The retried jobs (s6tr, q0xy, d5gk) are only the failure instances: they are cited as evidence and none is redone.

defaults_applied.how: The fix is at plan construction and its check, covering the whole class.
New unit tests plus fmt, clippy and test criteria.
Criteria run tests that fail before the change and pass after.
One focused change, mostly in plan.rs.
The criteria check that order follows owner priority.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Audience: the owner and operator who read the plan and queue, and the verifier. Goal: a stated owner priority reliably moves work to the front.

Repository already has Priority (urgent/high/normal/low), an effective-priority fixpoint in Plan::build, and `athena priority` records. The gap is the addendum-derived input and the order-versus-priority check. I did not read BRIEF.md or the addendum parsing, so that is an assumption.
Job 20261016-071159-s6tr (landed, pass): its findings were about xtask deps, the walltime measure and a cache nit. They are unrelated to the cause and no longer apply, so they are not touched.
Job 20261016-071202-q0xy (failed): its athena.toml `[parallel]` parse refusal is a separate config-schema failure and is not part of this cause. It is left unaddressed here.
Job 20261017-003902-d5gk (landed, pass): its findings concern CI result parsing and the unwired resolve. They are unrelated to ordering and are not touched.
Tests are added in plan.rs's own test module, so no governance files change.

acceptance_criteria.text: The change description names the root cause (owner priority from addenda is not an input to plan ordering and the order is never checked against it) and the fix sits in crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs, not in one job's request.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core plan`: a new test builds a plan where an addendum-stated top priority belongs to a newer, later-rung item and asserts it is in the first wave. The same test fails when the change is reverted.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core plan`: a new test asserts the order check reports a plan whose top-priority item is not first, and passes a correctly ordered plan. It covers the general case with several items, not one job's ids.
Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test`: all pass, with the existing plan ordering tests (dependencies first, effective priority) unchanged.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry that states the cause and the new check, for an outside reader.

out_of_scope: The CI routing build and walltime work from jobs s6tr and d5gk
The `[parallel]` config schema failure from job q0xy
Rewriting existing past plans or records
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower acceptance than the reference: the cause text is abstract and the existing priority machinery means the producer must find the actual gap.
urgent_reason: The request is marked urgent. Fixing this cause removes repeated hand rescues and misordered plans, which cuts thrash and wasted retries.
